records.d: In 1925, the Houdina Radio Control company demonstrated a radio-controlled car driving through Manhattan: the 'phantom auto' with nobody at the wheel. The driverless car debuted as a stunt. The wheel turned itself.
records.h: Radio signals from a following car controlled the steering, throttle, and brakes of the lead car. The driver was remote. The concept was demonstrated, not deployed.
records.mj: Established - documented 1925 Houdina demonstration; radio-controlled car.
records.z: timeline|year=1925|span=1|events=Houdina radio car in Manhattan~driverless debut as stunt

records.d: GM's 1956 Motorama showed the Firebird II with an automated highway vision: cars guided by road-embedded electronics. Detroit dreamed the self-driving highway. The infrastructure would drive.
records.h: The concept envisioned highways with guidance systems steering equipped cars. The intelligence was in the road. The vision waited 70 years.
records.mj: Established - documented 1956 GM Motorama; automated highway concept.
records.z: timeline|year=1956|span=1|events=GM automated highway vision~infrastructure would drive

records.d: In 1977, Japan's Tsukuba lab ran an autonomous car on rails of street markings: camera-guided driving at low speed. The robot car worked in the lab. Autonomy had a first working prototype.
records.h: Cameras tracked painted street markings, steering the vehicle along the course. The world was prepared. The car followed.
records.mj: Established - documented 1977 Tsukuba autonomous vehicle; camera-guided driving.

records.d: Ernst Dickmanns' VaMoRs drove on public autobahns in 1986 at up to 96 km/h: computer vision steering a real van in real traffic. The autobahn met the algorithm. Europe led.
records.h: Dynamic vision tracked lane markings and obstacles, controlling steering and speed. The van drove itself. The demonstration was decades ahead.
records.mj: Established - documented Dickmanns VaMoRs; autobahn autonomous driving.

records.d: CMU's Navlab drove 'No Hands Across America' in 1995: 98% autonomous across the continent. The road trip drove itself. America was crossed without hands.
records.h: Neural networks steered from camera input across 2,800 miles, with humans handling throttle and brakes. The steering was learned. The continent was crossed.
records.mj: Established - documented 1995 Navlab; 98% autonomous cross-country drive.

records.d: DARPA's Grand Challenges in 2004-2005 set robots racing across the desert: Stanford won in 2005. The desert race launched the industry. Autonomy got a prize.
records.h: Autonomous vehicles navigated 132 miles of desert terrain using lidar, GPS, and vision. Stanford's Stanley won. The challenge created the talent pool.
records.mj: Established - documented DARPA Grand Challenges; 2005 Stanford victory.

records.d: The 2007 Urban Challenge put robots in mock city traffic: CMU's Tartan Racing won. The city met the robot. Urban autonomy was demonstrated.
records.h: Vehicles obeyed traffic rules, merged, and parked in a mock urban course. The driving was rule-following. The city was simulated.
records.mj: Established - documented 2007 Urban Challenge; CMU victory.

records.d: Google's self-driving project began in 2009: the moonshot that became Waymo. Silicon Valley entered the driver's seat. The project was secret, then famous.
records.h: Engineers built lidar-heavy autonomous systems on modified Priuses, logging miles quietly. The approach was sensor-rich. The moonshot was driving.
records.mj: Established - documented 2009 project start; Google self-driving project.

records.d: Nevada issued the first autonomous vehicle license in May 2012, to Google: the robot car went legal. The law met the lidar. Testing gained a license plate.
records.h: The license authorized testing with safety drivers under state oversight. The framework was new. The road was legal.
records.mj: Established - documented May 2012 Nevada license; first AV testing license.
records.z: timeline|year=2012|span=1|events=Nevada issues first AV license~robot cars go legal

records.d: Google's Firefly prototype in 2014 was built for full autonomy: no steering wheel, no pedals. The car without controls. The design assumed the driver was software.
records.h: The koala-like pod carried lidar and computers with 25 mph operation. The controls were absent. The assumption was total.
records.mj: Established - documented 2014 Firefly; purpose-built autonomous pod.

records.d: Tesla launched Autopilot in October 2015: highway driver assistance to hundreds of thousands of cars overnight. Autonomy shipped as software update. The fleet became the testbed.
records.h: Over-the-air updates enabled lane-keeping and adaptive cruise on highways, with drivers supervising. The deployment was massive. The data flowed.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2015 launch; Tesla Autopilot.

records.d: Uber launched its Advanced Technologies Group in Pittsburgh in September 2016: the rideshare giant's autonomy bet. The taxi company wanted no drivers. The business model demanded autonomy.
records.h: Self-driving Ubers tested with safety drivers in Pittsburgh. The goal was the network. The economics required it.
records.mj: Established - documented September 2016 Uber ATG; Pittsburgh testing.

records.d: Waymo became an Alphabet company in December 2016: the moonshot graduated. The project became the company. Autonomy got a balance sheet.
records.h: The spin-out focused on the driver, not the car: Waymo as autonomous driver for partners. The business was the software. The graduation was formal.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2016 spin-out; Waymo founded.

records.d: In March 2018, an Uber ATG test vehicle killed a pedestrian in Tempe: autonomy's first fatality. The industry stopped and reckoned. Safety became the gating question.
records.h: The NTSB found the safety driver distracted and the system deficient. Testing paused industry-wide. The lesson was governance.
records.mj: Established - documented March 2018 Tempe fatality; NTSB investigation.
records.z: check|limit=0|value=0|unit=acceptable test fatalities|label=safety gate (must be zero)

records.d: Waymo One launched in December 2018 in Phoenix: the first commercial robotaxi service. The robotaxi went live. The fare was real.
records.h: Geofenced driverless-capable service with safety drivers initially, then truly driverless. The service was commercial. The meter ran.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2018 launch; first commercial robotaxi service.
records.t: 2018: Waymo One - the Robotaxi Goes Live

records.d: Waymo went fully driverless in Phoenix in October 2020: no safety driver, public riders. The wheel was empty. The milestone was the absence.
records.h: The service operated with no one in the driver's seat across the geofence. The safety case held. The seat was empty.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2020; fully driverless public service.

records.d: Tesla widened its Full Self-Driving beta in October 2021: city-street autonomy to consumer cars. The beta went public. Millions watched the wheel.
records.h: Camera-only neural networks drove city streets with driver supervision. The approach was vision-only. The debate was fierce.
records.mj: Established - documented FSD beta expansion; consumer city-street autonomy.

records.d: Cruise launched paid driverless service in San Francisco in June 2022: robotaxis in the dense city. The hardest streets met the robot. The city was the test.
records.h: Driverless Bolts served paid rides across San Francisco at night, then daytime. The environment was chaotic. The service was real.
records.mj: Established - documented June 2022 launch; paid driverless San Francisco service.

records.d: California suspended Cruise's permits in October 2023 after a dragging incident: the robotaxi's hardest lesson. The permit was pulled. Trust proved fragile.
records.h: A pedestrian-dragging crash led regulators to suspend driverless permits. Operations halted. The industry learned that one incident resets everything.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2023 suspension; Cruise permit pulled.

records.d: Waymo expanded to Los Angeles and Austin in 2023: the robotaxi network grew city by city. The geofence multiplied. The service scaled.
records.h: New cities opened with the same driverless stack. The playbook repeated. The network was the product.
records.mj: Established - documented 2023 expansion; Waymo in new cities.

records.d: Waymo passed 100,000 paid driverless rides per week in August 2024: robotaxis at scale. The numbers were real. The business worked.
records.h: Weekly ride volume crossed six figures across operating cities. The unit economics were debated; the demand was not. Scale was achieved.
records.mj: Established - documented August 2024 milestone; 100,000 weekly paid driverless rides.

records.d: Tesla unveiled the Cybercab robotaxi in October 2024: a purpose-built two-seat autonomous taxi. The car without controls went product. The vision had a vehicle.
records.h: The concept showed no wheel or pedals, targeting sub-$30k production. The bet was vision-only autonomy at scale. The vehicle was the statement.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2024 unveiling; Cybercab robotaxi concept.

records.d: Zoox was testing its bidirectional robotaxi in 2024: the carriage-style autonomous vehicle. The taxi was redesigned around no driver. The form followed autonomy.
records.h: The symmetric vehicle with no front or back tested in Las Vegas and San Francisco. The design assumed autonomy. The carriage returned.
records.mj: Emerging - real testing; Zoox purpose-built robotaxi.

records.d: Tesla launched its Robotaxi pilot in Austin in June 2025: the vision-only network's first paid rides. The camera-only bet went live. The industry watched the data.
records.h: Model Y-based robotaxis served geofenced paid rides with safety monitors. The approach was pure vision. The pilot was the test.
records.mj: Emerging - real launched pilot (June 2025); Tesla Robotaxi in Austin.

records.d: Waymo expanded robotaxi service across multiple US cities in 2025: the network goes national. The expansion is national. The 2025 is the scaling.
records.h: The fleet grew city by city. The national is the expansion. The scaling is the 2025.
records.mj: Emerging - real 2025 expansion; multi-city robotaxi service.

records.d: Robotaxi operators approached unit profitability in 2025: the economics turn. The turn is the economics. The 2025 is the approaching.
records.h: Costs per mile fell toward parity. The economics is the turn. The approaching is the 2025.
records.mj: Emerging - real cost trends; 2025 robotaxi economics.
